control_device_fabrication: Using a parameter-driven approach, we have engineered a perovskite solar cell that was crafted, thus realizing a PCE of 16.392%, FF of 76.125%, Voc of 1.008 V, and Jsc of 21.362 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 (1.73 mol/L) perovskite precursor solution was prepared. Different concentrations of Me-2PACz were added into the perovskite precursor solution for modification. The addition of MACl (5.0 mg/mL) was instrumental in fine-tuning the perovskite film's optical properties. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. A gentle antisolvent drop of 160 µL at last 6 s guided the perovskite crystals into a more ideal arrangement. Thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min improved crystal ordering and reduced defect density.
target_device_fabrication: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 19.1462%, with a VOC of 1.0556 V, FF of 73.7144%, and JSC of 24.6054 mA/cm². The perovskite composition of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L. The addition of Me-2PACz (0.33 mg/mL) as a SAM was performed to optimize surface passivation and ensure improved interface quality. 5.0 mg/mL of PSP was added. For perovskite films fabrication, the perovskite precursor was spin-coated on the as prepared substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s, subsequently at 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the second spin-coating step, 160 µL of CB was quickly poured onto the substrate after 6. The as-coated film was then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
